t.3.76.1: Bṛhadaśva said: Then, having passed that night, King Nala, finely adorned and accompanied by Vaidarbhī, saw the lord of the earth in the early morning.
t.3.76.2: Then Nala, composed and reverent, respectfully saluted his father-in-law, and after him the lovely Damayantī paid homage to her father.
t.3.76.3: Bhīma received him like a son with the greatest joy, and having honored him as was fitting, the lord then comforted Damayantī, the devoted wife, who was there together with Nala.
t.3.76.5: Then there arose in the city a very great sound of joy from the delighted people, on seeing Nala come back in such a state.
t.3.76.4: King Nala accepted that honor in due form, and in return he duly offered him his own respectful service.
t.3.76.6: And he adorned the city, garlanded with banners and flags; the royal roads were then made sprinkled, swept clean, and rich with flowers.
t.3.76.7: At every door of the townspeople flower decorations were arranged, and all the shrines of the gods were worshipped.
t.3.76.8: Ṛtuparṇa too heard that Nala, who had been disguised as Bāhuka, was reunited with Damayantī, and the lord of men rejoiced.
t.3.76.9: Having had him brought before him, King Nala begged the king's forgiveness; and he, esteemed for his wisdom, in turn begged Nala's forgiveness, giving his reasons.
t.3.76.10: That king, duly honored and filled with wonder, greeted the Naiṣadha joyfully, saying, "By good fortune you are reunited with your own wife!"
t.3.76.11: I hope I have not committed any offense against you, Naiṣadha, while you were dwelling unrecognized in my house, lord of Niṣadha?
t.3.76.12: Whatever wrongful deeds I may have done, whether knowingly or unknowingly, you ought to forgive me for them.
t.3.76.13: You have not done me even the slightest wrong, O king; and even if you had, I would feel no anger, for I must forgive you.
t.3.76.14: For you were already my friend and my kinsman, O lord of men; from now on, you should bring me even greater joy.
t.3.76.15: Well provided with every object of desire, I have lived happily with you, O king; never have I lived so happily in my own house as I always did in yours.
t.3.76.16: And this knowledge of horses, which is yours, still resides in me; I wish to hand it over to you, O king, if you think it fit.
t.3.76.17: Having spoken thus, the Naiṣadha gave the knowledge to Ṛtuparṇa, and he received it by the rite prescribed by the ordinance.
t.3.76.18: Then King Bhāṅgasvari, having received the secret of horses, took another charioteer and went back to his own city.
t.3.76.19: When Ṛtuparṇa had gone back, O lord of the people, King Nala dwelt in the city of Kuṇḍina for a time that seemed not very long.
